newsitem.title: USA: GE sees big savings from quality program - CEO.
newsitem.headline: GE sees big savings from quality program - CEO.

text.p: General Electric Co chief executive Jack Welch said a company-wide quality improvement program called Six Sigma would yield $550 million to $600 million in savings this year.

Welch told shareholders GE would spend $400 million in 1997 on Sigma Six, a program aimed at vastly reducing errors in GE's products and services. He said all GE managers would have to complete training in Six Sigma techniques by the end of 1998.
"The snowball is growing, and by 2000 the cumulative bottom-line impact of Six Sigma quality will be measured not in hundreds of thousands or millions but in billions" of dollars, Welch said.

In other matters, shareholders approved a two-for-one stock split during the meeting at the Charlotte Convention Center. The split is expected to become effective on April 28, according to the company's proxy statement for the meeting.
Shareholders also authorized a doubling to 4.4 billion in GE's common share base. Certificates representing the new shares will be mailed to stockholders in early May, the company said.
